secretin

HCO₃⁻ water Cl⁻ H⁺ secretin cAMP proenzyme (tab) active enzyme

Hover or focus a part for a short explanation. Switch secretin off: CFTR shuts, less HCO₃⁻ and water reach the duodenum, and the acid is left over.

Sources

Educational only, not medical advice. Schematic, not to scale: one duct cell stands for the duct, and speeds, counts and levels are illustrative (a qualitative model, not measurements). On a phone, tap a part to read about it. This is a simplified version of the detailed figure (open the detailed figure). No measured value is shown; every level is qualitative.

  • Duct cell (panel A). Secretin receptor and cAMP/PKA signalling, CFTR, the SLC26A6 Cl⁻/HCO₃⁻ exchanger, AQP1, and the HCO₃⁻ routes named in the hover text: Lee MG et al., Molecular mechanism of pancreatic and salivary gland fluid and HCO₃⁻ secretion, Physiol Rev 2012;92:39-74 (PMID 22298651). Background and the secretin-to-duodenum link: Pandol SJ, The Exocrine Pancreas, Morgan & Claypool 2010 (NCBI Bookshelf NBK54128).
  • CFTR location. Marino et al., Localization of the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator in pancreas, J Clin Invest 1991;88:712-6 (PMID 1713921): human pancreas, apical membrane of centroacinar and intralobular duct cells, no conclusive staining of acinar cells.
  • Duodenum (panel B). Enteropeptidase in the brush border, cleavage of trypsinogen's activation peptide, and trypsin's activation of the other proenzymes: Zheng XL, Kitamoto Y, Sadler JE, Enteropeptidase, a type II transmembrane serine protease, Front Biosci (Elite Ed) 2009;1:242-9 (PMID 19482641). Amylase and lipase secreted active, proteases as proenzymes: Fieker et al., Clin Exp Gastroenterol 2011 (PMID 21753892).

Simplified. One duct cell stands for the duct; positions, counts and speeds are illustrative and time is compressed. Left out of the drawing (named in the hover text or in the detailed figure only): other transporters, gene names, transport ratios, signalling intermediates, neighbouring cells and the individual enzymes.
